content.value_statement: Python data contracts can drift when inputs come from APIs, files, or users. This skill gives concise Pydantic v2 patterns for validation, serialization, and error handling.
actual_capabilities: Shows BaseModel definitions with typed fields, defaults, and optional values.
Demonstrates model_validate, model_validate_json, model_dump, and model_dump_json.
Covers Field constraints, aliases, SecretStr, ConfigDict, and strict models.
Explains field_validator, model_validator, and ValidationError handling patterns.
Includes examples for nested models, enums, TypeAdapter, and JSON schema generation.
limitations: It is a reference guide, not an executable Pydantic tool.
It does not cover every Pydantic v2 API or migration detail.
Examples use simplified validation and may need production hardening.
It does not install packages or verify local environment compatibility.

use_cases.title: Create API Data Models
use_cases.description: Define typed request and response models with defaults, constraints, and validation errors.

use_cases.title: Validate Pipeline Records
use_cases.description: Model nested records, standalone lists, enum values, and schema output for data workflows.

use_cases.title: Improve Serialization Rules
use_cases.description: Control which fields are dumped, hidden, aliased, or converted for client output.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Pydantic skill to design a Pydantic v2 model for a user profile with required fields, defaults, and clear validation behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Add Field Constraints
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Pydantic skill to add field constraints, aliases, strict settings, and helpful validation errors to this data model description.

prompt_templates.title: Design Nested Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Pydantic skill to model nested objects, lists, enum values, and standalone TypeAdapter validation for this data shape.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a Pydantic Schema
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the Pydantic skill to review this Pydantic v2 design for strict configuration, serialization control, custom validators, and error handling gaps.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a model that validates product records with price and website fields.
output_examples.output: The response recommends typed fields, Field constraints, aliases, EmailStr, HttpUrl, defaults, and excluded internal fields.

output_examples.input: A user needs to explain validation failures to API clients.
output_examples.output: The response describes ValidationError handling, error counts, field locations, messages, and stable user-facing summaries.

output_examples.input: A user wants safer serialization for account data.
output_examples.output: The response suggests SecretStr, excluded fields, include and exclude options, JSON mode dumps, and alias-based output.

best_practices: Use specific field types and constraints instead of broad primitive types.
Set ConfigDict options when strictness, aliases, or assignment validation matter.
Handle ValidationError output deliberately before showing errors to users.
anti_patterns: Do not rely on automatic coercion when exact input types are required.
Do not serialize secrets or internal fields without explicit exclude rules.
Do not place complex business logic inside validators without tests.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps create Pydantic v2 models, validators, serialization rules, and error handling patterns for Python projects.

faq.question: Does it execute Python code?
faq.answer: No. The skill is documentation and guidance. It does not run code or install packages by itself.

faq.question: Can it help with nested data?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes examples for nested models, lists, optional relationships, and enum-backed fields.

faq.question: Does it cover serialization controls?
faq.answer: Yes. It shows model_dump options, SecretStr, excluded fields, aliases, and JSON-compatible output.

faq.question: Is it only for web APIs?
faq.answer: No. The patterns also apply to data pipelines, configuration objects, scripts, and service boundaries.

faq.question: What Pydantic version does it target?
faq.answer: It targets Pydantic v2 and uses v2 APIs such as model_validate, model_dump, and ConfigDict.
